content.user_title: Build Responsive Drag and Swipe Interactions
content.value_statement: Gesture interfaces can lag behind touch input, jump on release, or conflict with scrolling. This skill guides direct tracking, velocity-aware release, and interruptible interactions.
actual_capabilities: Explain direct pointer tracking with motion values or element transforms instead of per-move React state updates.
Guide distance-based and velocity-based dismissal using Motion drag event properties.
Show how to derive overlay opacity from drawer position with linked motion values.
Recommend Vaul for sheets and describe transition timing and interactive child exclusions.
Describe interruptible release motion, drag elasticity, and hold-to-confirm timing.
Provide touch target, scrolling, hover, real-device testing, and reduced-motion guidance.
limitations: Provides instructions and illustrative snippets, not a complete application or standalone gesture library.
Examples focus on Motion, React, CSS, and Vaul rather than native mobile frameworks.
Requires project-specific integration and real-device testing; the skill includes no automated test suite.
References companion skills that are not included in this single-file package.

use_cases.title: Improve swipe dismissal
use_cases.description: Refine a swipeable card with direct tracking, fast-flick dismissal, and quick snap-back when release thresholds are not met.

use_cases.title: Review mobile drawer behavior
use_cases.description: Evaluate drawer timing, overlay synchronization, touch targets, interactive children, and reduced-motion behavior before release.

use_cases.title: Diagnose gesture regressions
use_cases.description: Use the touch checklist to investigate scroll conflicts, accidental drags, interrupted animations, and differences between desktop simulation and phones.

prompt_templates.title: Understand gesture phases
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain tracking and release phases for a swipeable card. Identify when direct movement, springs, and velocity should apply.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: learn the core interaction model.

prompt_templates.title: Add swipe dismissal
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Motion component: [component]. Add distance-based and velocity-based swipe dismissal, drag resistance, and quick snap-back without per-move React state.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: improve an existing gesture component.

prompt_templates.title: Refine a Vaul drawer
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Vaul drawer: [component]. Check overlay progress, interactive child exclusions, floating-drawer timing, touch targets, and reduced-motion behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose interrupted gestures
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this gesture implementation and recording observations: [details]. Diagnose lag, release jumps, and interruption failures. Propose focused changes and real-phone regression checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: investigate performance and interaction failures.

output_examples.input: My swipeable card follows the pointer slowly and ignores quick flicks.
output: Tracking: update a motion value or the element transform directly, without easing or per-move React state.
Release: evaluate both travel distance and release velocity before dismissing.
Cancellation: return quickly with a spring when neither threshold is met.

output_examples.input: Buttons inside my small Vaul drawer trigger dragging, and the drawer feels slow.
output: Exclude interactive children from dragging with the Vaul no-drag attribute.
For a small floating drawer, consider approximately 200 milliseconds instead of the full-sheet 500-millisecond timing.
Keep overlay, height, and content timing consistent, then verify touch behavior on a real phone.

output_examples.input: How should swipe interactions behave when reduced motion is enabled?
output_examples.output: Keep direct pointer tracking. Reduce momentum, bounce, and decorative movement. On release, use a short position or opacity change instead of a bouncy spring.

best_practices: Separate direct tracking from release physics and derive linked visuals from the same drag progress.
Prefer an established drawer library when it covers the interaction, and verify focus trapping and Escape dismissal.
Test on real phones with scrolling, interrupted gestures, interactive children, and reduced-motion settings.
anti_patterns: Apply a spring during pointer tracking or update React state for every pointer movement.
Dismiss only by distance while ignoring fast flicks and release velocity.
Use keyframe animations on draggable elements or animate linked overlays independently of drag progress.

faq.question: What does this skill provide?
faq.answer: It provides gesture design rules, Motion and CSS examples, Vaul recommendations, and touch and reduced-motion checklists.

faq.question: Does this skill install Motion or Vaul?
faq.answer: No. It recommends libraries and shows usage patterns, but includes no installation script or dependency configuration.

faq.question: When should I use Vaul instead of custom dragging?
faq.answer: Use Vaul for bottom sheets and drawers when it covers your needs. Build custom gestures for interactions without a suitable library.

faq.question: Why does my dragged element trail the pointer?
faq.answer: Tracking may use easing, a spring, per-move React state, or inherited CSS variables. Prefer direct motion values or element transforms.

faq.question: How does it address accessibility?
faq.answer: It covers touch targets, scroll coordination, hover gating, and reduced motion. It also highlights focus trapping and Escape dismissal for drawers.

faq.question: Does the skill verify behavior automatically?
faq.answer: No. It recommends real-phone testing and diagnostic checks, but includes no automated tests or device validation tools.
